parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with payroll, so the topic is shared. The problem is that the module does not use its own abstractions consistently. PayrollAuditService receives a PrismaService through its constructor, and trail() uses it (this.prisma). But log() ignores that dependency and runs `new PrismaClient()` on every call. That bypasses the injected abstraction, so connection handling, configuration and testability now differ between two methods of the same class. Data access is also inconsistent across the module: PayrollService works through the injected EmployeeRepository and TimesheetRepository and maps records into domain models (Timesheet, Employee, Payslip). PayrollAuditService instead calls the Prisma payrollAudit delegate directly, with no repository and no domain model, and it builds an ad-hoc id inline. The rubric fails a unit that bypasses its own abstractions, and the log() call does that without doubt. Import direction is out of scope and was not used in this judgment.

violations.message: log() creates its own `new PrismaClient()` instead of using the injected `this.prisma` (PrismaService). This bypasses the class's own dependency, and trail() in the same class uses the injected one.

Accesses data directly through the Prisma delegate (payrollAudit.create/findMany), while the module's other service uses repository abstractions and domain models. Data access is inconsistent within the module.
